ordered.title: Symptoms That Lead to Remanufactured Engine Replacement
ordered.description: Remanufactured engines are typically specified when the original engine has suffered a failure that requires full restoration to factory specification - often for commercial fleets, insurance jobs, or classic vehicles.

blocks.text: Catastrophic internal failure - no oil pressure, rod through block.
Head gasket failure, cracked block, water pump failure.
Bearing failure - often caused by oil starvation.
Worn piston rings, scored cylinder bores, valve stem seals.
⚠️ Engine management light with compression loss
Internal damage - valves, pistons, cylinder head.
Cracked block or failed main seal.
Turbo failure, injector failure, internal damage.

Insurers often specify remanufactured for like-new replacement.
The quality tier is justified by the vehicle value.
Remanufactured offers the longest usable life.
Remanufactured units meet original emissions standards.

ordered.title: What "Remanufactured" Actually Means
ordered.description: BS AU257:2002 - The British Standard for Remanufacturing

blocks.text: "A remanufactured engine is exactly that - an engine which has been returned to the manufacturer's specification to provide levels of performance and reliability equivalent to the original engine."

items: Full strip-down - Engine completely dismantled to component level.
Clean and inspect - All components cleaned, measured, and inspected.
Replace all wear components - Pistons, rings, bearings, seals, gaskets, timing components - all new.
Machine to original tolerances - Block, cylinder head, crankshaft, camshaft - all machined to factory spec.
Reassemble - Using new components and OEM-spec parts.
Test - Dyno-tested to ensure performance matches original engine.

blocks.text: [EM-QUOTE] based on supplier data. Remanufactured offers the best balance of quality and cost for many applications.

ordered.title: Why BS AU257:2002 Matters
ordered.description: BS AU257:2002 is the British Standard Code of Practice for the remanufacture of automotive components - specifically engines.

items: Manufacturer's specification: The engine must be returned to the original manufacturer's tolerances and specifications.
New components: All wearing components (pistons, rings, bearings, seals, gaskets) must be new - not reused.
Testing: The engine must be dyno-tested to ensure performance matches the original.
Traceability: All components must be traceable to source.
Quality management: The remanufacturer must have ISO 9001:2015 quality management.

rows: May or may not be tested
Must be tested to original spec

blocks.text: "We've been remanufacturing engines to BS AU257 for over 75 years. The standard exists because there was confusion in the market about what 'reconditioned' actually meant. When an engine carries BS AU257 certification, the customer knows exactly what they're getting - an engine that performs and lasts like the original."

cards.title: What is a remanufactured engine?
cards.text: What is a remanufactured engine? A remanufactured engine is returned to the manufacturer's original specification - providing levels of performance and reliability equivalent to the original engine. It is certified to BS AU257:2002, the British Standard for remanufacturing.
cards.fullText: What is a remanufactured engine? A remanufactured engine is returned to the manufacturer's original specification - providing levels of performance and reliability equivalent to the original engine. It is certified to BS AU257:2002, the British Standard for remanufacturing.

cards.title: How much does a remanufactured engine cost?
cards.text: How much does a remanufactured engine cost? Remanufactured engines cost £3,500-£6,500 supply only or £5,500-£9,000 fitted . That's 30-40% more than reconditioned, but 40% less than a new OEM engine.
cards.fullText: How much does a remanufactured engine cost? Remanufactured engines cost £3,500-£6,500 supply only or £5,500-£9,000 fitted . That's 30-40% more than reconditioned, but 40% less than a new OEM engine.

cards.title: What's the difference between remanufactured and reconditioned?
cards.text: What's the difference between remanufactured and reconditioned? A reconditioned engine has worn parts replaced and is made serviceable. A remanufactured engine is returned to factory specification, certified to BS AU257:2002, with all wear components new, machined to original factory tolerances, and tested to meet original performance.
cards.fullText: What's the difference between remanufactured and reconditioned? A reconditioned engine has worn parts replaced and is made serviceable. A remanufactured engine is returned to factory specification, certified to BS AU257:2002, with all wear components new, machined to original factory tolerances, and tested to meet original performance.

cards.title: What is BS AU257:2002?
cards.text: What is BS AU257:2002? BS AU257:2002 is the British Standard Code of Practice for the remanufacture of automotive components. It requires the engine to be returned to the manufacturer's original specification, with all wear components replaced and performance equivalent to the original.
cards.fullText: What is BS AU257:2002? BS AU257:2002 is the British Standard Code of Practice for the remanufacture of automotive components. It requires the engine to be returned to the manufacturer's original specification, with all wear components replaced and performance equivalent to the original.

cards.title: Who should buy a remanufactured engine?
cards.text: Who should buy a remanufactured engine? Commercial fleets (minimising downtime), classic car owners (preserving originality), insurance/warranty jobs (like-new replacement), and owners of very high-value vehicles (£30,000+).
cards.fullText: Who should buy a remanufactured engine? Commercial fleets (minimising downtime), classic car owners (preserving originality), insurance/warranty jobs (like-new replacement), and owners of very high-value vehicles (£30,000+).

cards.title: How long does a remanufactured engine take?
cards.text: How long does a remanufactured engine take? Lead time is typically 7-14 days . This includes sourcing a core, stripping, machining, rebuilding, and testing. Remanufacturers often hold stock of common engines.
cards.fullText: How long does a remanufactured engine take? Lead time is typically 7-14 days . This includes sourcing a core, stripping, machining, rebuilding, and testing. Remanufacturers often hold stock of common engines.

cards.title: What warranty comes with a remanufactured engine?
cards.text: What warranty comes with a remanufactured engine? Typically 12-24 months , parts and labour. This is equivalent to the warranty on a new engine - unlike reconditioned engines which typically have shorter warranties.
cards.fullText: What warranty comes with a remanufactured engine? Typically 12-24 months , parts and labour. This is equivalent to the warranty on a new engine - unlike reconditioned engines which typically have shorter warranties.

cards.title: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer?
cards.text: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? DVLA - update the engine number on your V5C registration document [DVLA, 2025]. Insurer - you should check with your insurer to ensure your policy reflects major mechanical replacements.
